title: Tunisian foundation row
subtitle: How to work the first forward pass that starts a Tunisian crochet piece
excerpt: The Tunisian foundation row picks up a full row of loops onto the hook in one pass, creating the starting fabric from which all further Tunisian stitches are worked.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book.

glossaryTerms.definition: In Tunisian crochet, the left-to-right movement along a row during which loops are picked up and accumulated on the hook without being worked off.
In Tunisian crochet, the right-to-left movement that works off the accumulated loops in pairs, completing the row.
The most basic Tunisian stitch, worked by inserting the hook through the front vertical bar of the stitch and drawing up a loop without working it off until the return pass.

content.text: Tunisian crochet uses a long hook to hold an entire row of loops at once, producing a dense, woven-looking fabric. The foundation row is the
first forward pass
: you work along the foundation chain picking up one loop per chain and holding them all on the hook, then complete the row with a
return pass
that works the loops off in pairs. After the foundation row, the working structure of each
Tunisian simple stitch
continues the same two-pass pattern.
What you need

items.name: Tunisian hook
items.note: A long hook or a hook with a cord extension. Must be at least as long as the number of stitches in the row.

content.text: Working the foundation forward pass
Work a foundation chain of the number of stitches stated in the pattern.
Insert the hook into the second chain from the hook (not the first). Yarn over and draw up a loop. Leave it on the hook.
Insert the hook into the next chain. Yarn over and draw up a loop. Leave it on the hook.
Repeat step 3 across every chain. At the end of the foundation chain, every stitch has a loop sitting on the hook.
Do not turn. The work stays flat and never turns in Tunisian crochet.
Working the foundation return pass
Yarn over and draw through the first loop on the hook.
Yarn over and draw through the next two loops on the hook. Repeat this step until one loop remains.
The single remaining loop is the starting loop for the next forward pass.
Common problems

items.symptom: The hook runs out of space before the forward pass is complete
items.cause: A standard short hook was used instead of a Tunisian hook.
items.fix: Use a Tunisian hook or a hook with a cable extension. The hook must be long enough to hold all the stitches for the row.

items.symptom: The fabric curls badly to one side
items.cause: Tunisian fabric naturally curls toward the wrong side due to the way loops are picked up. This is normal in a flat swatch.
items.fix: Blocking the finished piece corrects most curl. For projects in progress, the curl reduces as more rows are added.

content.text: What to try next

After the foundation row is stable, work the second row using Tunisian simple stitch: insert the hook through the front vertical bar of each stitch (not the chain loops) on the forward pass. See the return pass guide for how the second row return works.
